head: d4600fcba2c0d1db0c9a5aa6a4d4328c3be472a1
scope: PR169, usage reads that clear rejections. A foreground lane router on port 18797 had copies of the severus and personal logins and a planted weekly rejection on severus. The lane ran the installed router at the prior record first, and then this code, against the real usage endpoint. Real-account checks covered a new conversation, a resume, and a restart. The run built the code at d4600fc, which the rebase onto e560fe1 replaced with b3f6e25 at the same code digest. Unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun. The saved lane.py includes the restart phase, which was added after the route phase ran.

matrix.scenario: severus token is outside the four-hour refresh lead
personal token is outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code and executable match the build at d4600fc
The installed router at the prior record keeps a planted weekly rejection after its start read shows the window below its limit
A start read that shows the weekly window below its limit clears the planted weekly rejection, and the account is ready
A start read at the weekly limit keeps the weekly rejection, while the five-hour and Fable windows read 0
severus is admissible with paid overflow disabled
new receives a routed 200 on the cleared account
Resume preserves account and conversation content
After restart, the cleared rejection stays cleared
Restart preserves the served conversation's account and content
Identity is the same at the start and the end
Evidence contains no copied access token

detail.method: The scan looked for the sk-ant-, JWT, and Bearer token patterns. The run had already deleted the lane's login copies.

incidents: The first restart attempt was the fourth lane start in 21 s. Its start read of each account got 429 from the usage endpoint, with retry-after 4m57s, so no fresh usage reading arrived. The harness waited 120 s for that reading, then stopped the lane without sending the request. The daily router's next background read of the same two accounts also got 429, with retry-after 3m54s. Its retry read succeeded at 2026-11-12T19:53:29-08:00 (daily-429-events.jsonl). The restart step then ran once and passed.

The resume after the restart came 5 min 11 s after the previous request, past the 5-minute prompt-cache lifetime. That request therefore wrote the conversation's cache again on the same account (4,304 tokens).

prior_acceptance.status: historical reference, not rerun at this code
